foundry-obs-scene-switcher.settings.host: Hostname or IP of the machine running OBS. Usually 'localhost' if OBS is on the same computer as Foundry.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.settings.port: Port of OBS's WebSocket server (Tools → WebSocket Server Settings). Default is 4455.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.settings.pass: Password shown in OBS's WebSocket Server Settings. Leave blank if authentication is disabled.
OBS rejected this password ({reason}). Copy it exactly from OBS → Tools → WebSocket Server Settings → Show Connect Info.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.settings.over: Show the current character's portrait and stats on stream, via an OBS Browser Source. Configure it under 'Character Overlay' below.

In OBS: Sources → + → Browser, tick 'Local file', and browse to this file inside your Foundry user data folder (its location is shown in Setup → Configuration). Size the source around 480 × 220. It has to be the local file, not a web address: Foundry deliberately serves module HTML as plain text, so a Browser Source pointed at the server shows the markup instead of the card.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.settings.chat: Show the tail of the chat log on stream, via an OBS Browser Source. Your players' messages always appear; choose which of your own do, under 'Character Overlay' below. Whispers and blind rolls are never sent.

In OBS: Sources → + → Browser, tick 'Local file', and browse to this file inside your Foundry user data folder (its location is shown in Setup → Configuration). Around 380 × 500 suits a side column. It has to be the local file, not a web address.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.settings.comb: Show the turn order on stream, via an OBS Browser Source, with whoever is up highlighted. It uses the same privacy rules as the character card, and hides itself when combat ends.

In OBS: Sources → + → Browser, tick 'Local file', and browse to this file inside your Foundry user data folder (its location is shown in Setup → Configuration). Around 320 × 420 suits a side column. It has to be the local file, not a web address.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.settings.brow: Browser Source file path copied to the clipboard.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.overlay.menuH: Choose what the on-stream character card shows and get the Browser Source URL for OBS.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.overlay.title: OBS Character Overlay
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.overlay.intro: Puts a card on your stream showing whichever character the scene switcher is currently on — the token you have selected, or the combatant whose turn it is.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.overlay.urlHi: In OBS, add a Browser Source, tick 'Local file', and browse to this file inside your Foundry user data folder (Setup → Configuration shows where that is). Around 480×220 is a good size. It must be the local file rather than a web address — Foundry serves module HTML as plain text on purpose, so a Browser Source pointed at the server would show the markup instead of the card. 'Shutdown source when not visible' is fine to leave ticked; the card refills within a few seconds of the scene becoming visible.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.overlay.rowsH: Player characters and NPCs get their own sets, so a villain can appear with a portrait and name while their stats stay at the table. The name is always shown. Rows with no data for a given character are hidden automatically, whatever is ticked here.
A blanket rule. Individual NPCs can also be ticked in Scene Mappings, and those appear whatever is chosen here. Player characters always appear; tokens hidden from players never do.
Only NPCs with a scene mapping
Any NPC (puts every monster's stats on stream)
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.overlay.event: The browser event this module sends to OBS. Only change this if you are writing your own overlay page — then add '?event=yourName' to the Browser Source URL.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.chat.urlHint: A second Browser Source, again as a local file. Around 380 × 500 suits a column down one side of the scene.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.chat.hint: Messages your players write always reach the stream — they are the players' own words, in a log the whole table can already read. These choose which of your own messages do, because as Gamemaster you are also the author of every monster's attack roll and every module's status card. Whispers and blind rolls are never sent, whatever is ticked here.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.chat.category: Initiative, attacks and saves you roll — including every NPC's, since you are the one rolling them.
Messages you post while speaking as an NPC.
Scene description and stage direction posted with /emote.
Table talk you post as yourself rather than as a character.
Everything else that lands in the log under your name — item cards, module notices, update banners. Usually the noisiest option.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.chat.linesHin: How many of the most recent messages the panel keeps. Older ones scroll off.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.combat.urlHin: A third Browser Source, again as a local file. Around 320 × 420 suits a column down one side of the scene. The panel hides itself when there is no combat.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.config.menuHi: Map actors to OBS scenes and set the exploration and DM fallback scenes.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.config.title: OBS Scene Mappings
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.config.intro: Map actors to OBS scene names. During combat, the focused token (or the current turn's combatant) picks the scene. If OBS is connected, scene names auto-complete from your live scene list.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.config.explor: Shown whenever combat is not active.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.config.dmFall: Shown during combat when no mapping matches the focused token or current combatant.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.config.actorM: Leave blank to use the DM fallback scene for that actor.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.config.cardCo: Card puts that character on the stream overlay when the module is on them, with no scene switch — useful for naming a recurring NPC while you keep scene changes for the big moments. Player characters always get a card. Needs the Stream Character Overlay switched on.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.config.cardAl: Player characters always appear on the overlay.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.config.noActo: No actors exist in this world yet.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.button.toolti: Toggle automatic OBS scene switching. When off, OBS is left alone so you can control scenes manually.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.button.proble: OBS scene switching is enabled but not working: {reason}. Click to toggle sync; check the module settings to fix the connection.
foundry-obs-scene-switcher.notify.connec: OBS Scene Switcher: could not connect to OBS ({error}). Check host/port/password in the module settings.
